RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the March 4, 2003/Phalguna 13, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Civil Aviation; Finance and Company Affairs; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—20
Loans for self-employment schemes
by banks
*181. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY:
SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during the
recent Conference of the State Ministers
of Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and
Public Works, it was highlighted that the
Nationalised Banks were sitting tight on
loan applications for self-employment
schemes in rural areas and this was
hampering the rural development;
(b) if so, Government's response
thereto; and
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
in order to expedite the release of bank
loans for self-employment projects in the
rural sector?
Amount received through Hawala
Channel
*182. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
estimated the amount received through
Hawala Channel in the country during the
last three years, year-wise;
(b) whether Government propose to
bring about changes in the Foreign
Contributions Regulations Act, to monitor
and control such receipts; and
(c) if so, what are the details in this
regard?
Psychological tests to Air Traffic
Controllers
*183. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Air Traffic Controllers
undergo any psychological tests;
(b) if so, the key areas they are tested in;
(c) if not, whether there is any need
for the Air Traffic Controllers to undergo
psychological tests since they face pressure
situations daily;
(d) whether it is a fact that many a
times Air Traffic Controllers have to take
risk in regard to their jobs to avoid major
mishaps; and
(e) whether Air Traffic Controllers
undergo some training overseas to learn
new and advanced techniques for Air
Traffic handling?

Tunnel connecting the Red fort to the
Dilli Chalo Park
*184. PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM:
Will the Minister of TOURISM AND
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
plans to open 200 year old tunnel
connecting the Red Fort to the Dilli Chalo
Park and the Ring Road behind the Fort;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether Government have
identified such tunnels used by the ancient
monarchs in other States;
(d) if so, the details thereof,  State-
wise; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Full convertibility of rupee
†*185. SHRI GHULAM NABI
AZAD:
SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
any steps aimed at eventually making the
rupee fully convertible and ease controls
on investment abroad by mutual funds and
individuals; and
(b) if so, broad features thereof?
Tax amnesty scheme for raising funds
for infrastructure sector
*186. SHRI  PRITHVIRAJ  CHAVAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering a new tax amnesty scheme to
raise long term funds in the infrastructure
sector; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Involvement of NGOs in rain water
harnessing in Karnataka
*187. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Karnataka Government has
sought the involvement of Non-
Government and Voluntary Organisations
for harnessing rain water;
(b) if so, the number of Non-
Government and voluntary organisations
proposed to be involved for the purpose;
(c) whether there is any provision in
the Central scheme for recharge of ground
water for the involvement of NG and
voluntary organisations; and
(d) if so, whether Government have
given permission to Karnataka
Government to involve them in harnessing
rain water?
Loss due to sharing of Ravi waters to
Pakistan
†*188. SHRI BALKAVI BAIRAGI:
Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Water
of Ravi river has been flowing incessantly
to Pakistan even after 50 years of
Independence;
(b) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the book "Troubled water
of Punjab" by Vijai Pal Singh in which it
has been explained about the rivers of
Punjab and highlighted as to how India is
losing to Pakistan on sharing river water;
and
(c) if so, the details of the steps taken
by Government in this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Leasing of shops at airports
1232. SHRI S.M. LAL JAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any policy
regarding leasing out of space for shops at
airports by the Airports Authority of India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that such shops
charge high prices for consumables; and
(d) whether it is also a fact that there is
no control of AAI regarding the prices they
charge from passengers?
Enhancing seat capacity on
international routes
1233. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that while the
availability of seats on the main routes is
slowly decreasing, Government's open sky
policy to opermit more international
airlines to opperate on these sectors has
failed to take off;
(b) whether it is a fact that while there
is a poor response from the US and Europe
carriers, others are willing to increase their
flights on these routes; and
(c) if so, the details of plan to increase
its capacity on international flights?
Separate company for ground
handling operations by AI
1234. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA :
SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
create a separate subsidiary of Air India
for its ground handling operations;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
by Government to prepare a financial
restructuring strategy for Air India in order
to bring it out of red?
Enquiring by DGCA
1235. SHRI R.K. ANAND:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned
"Close call in mid-air near Mumbai
Airport" which appeared in The Hindustan
Times of 3rd January 2003;

276
WIN2\SESSION\7741RS.pm5 276
(b) if so, whether an enquiry was
ordered by the DGCA in this regard;
(c) if so, the details of the enquiry
report; and
(d) the action taken by Government so
that mid-air collisions does not occur in
future?
Reduction in air fare
1236. SHRI AIMADUDDIN AHMED
KHAN (DURRU):
SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal under
Government's consideration to bring down
the domestic as well as the international
air fare;
(b) whether another proposal has been
mooted to abolish the 15 per cent Inland
Travel Tax for all domestic carrier;
(c) if so, the details in this regard; and
(d) by when these measures are likely
to take concrete shape?
Losses by AI and IA
1237. SHRI BHAGATRAM
MAHNAR:
SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned "IA
continues to be in the red" which appeared
in The Hindustan Times, New Delhi on the
2nd November, 2002;
(b) if so, what are the details of losses
being incurred by Indian Airlines and Air
India during the last two years; and
(c) what are the reasons for losses by
these airlines during the last two years and
the steps being taken to make these airlines
profitable?
Revenue sharing between
AI and IA
1238. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that both Air India
and Indian Airlines ply some flights on
common international routes and also
offer seats under bilateral agreements to
foreign airlines;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Air
India earns Rs. 246 crore from commercial
and royalty arrangements while Indian
Airlines gets Rs. 10 crore only; and
(c) if so, what steps are being taken to
grant Indian Airlines a larger share of
earnings from bilateral agreements with
foreign carriers?
DGCA's  instructions on
cockpit doors
1239. PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Director-General of
Civil Aviation's  instruction to airlines to
change their cockpit doors by April, 2003,
after the 9/11, has been implemented;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) what are the other instructions of
the DGCA which are to be followed or
implemented by the Ministry?

reduce its large aircraft acquisition order
